blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **уходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **уходить** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уйти**. present: я ухожу́ · ты ухо́дишь · он ухо́дит · мы ухо́дим · вы ухо́дите · они ухо́дят. — Wiktionary, «уходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't seem to be leaving.
exercises.context: **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **заходите** is the present tense (2nd person plural) of **заходить** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **зайти**. present: я захожу́ · ты захо́дишь · он захо́дит · мы захо́дим · вы захо́дите · они захо́дят. — Wiktionary, «заходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **входить** (the infinitive) (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **войти**. — Wiktionary, «входить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  Compare: «Я вхожу в эту комнату каждый день.» (Imperfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я входил в эту комнату каждый день.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **сошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **сойти** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сходить**. past: он сошёл · она сошла́ · оно сошло́ · они сошли́. — Wiktionary, «сойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **сойти**: to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from; to pass by; (figuratively) to pass for, to be taken for.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. (DLI, Lesson 79)

exercises.why: **выходить** (the infinitive) (to go out, to come out, to walk out; to withdraw, to retire) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **выйти**. — Wiktionary, «выходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't want to go out.
exercises.context: **вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **переносил** is the past tense (masculine) of **переносить** (to transfer, to carry, to transport (somewhere)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **перенести**. past: он переноси́л · она переноси́ла · оно переноси́ло · они переноси́ли. — Wiktionary, «переносить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **переносить**: to transfer, to carry, to transport (somewhere); to carry over (a word) to the next line; to postpone, to put off; to extend (to).  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Переносить — перенести — to carry over (on foot), to move; to endure.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. (DLI, Lesson 79)

exercises.why: **расходится** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **расходиться** (to go away, to disperse (in different directions), to spread; to break up (of a crowd, meeting, etc.)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **разойтись**. present: я расхожу́сь · ты расхо́дишься · он расхо́дится · мы расхо́димся · вы расхо́дитесь · они расхо́дятся. — Wiktionary, «расходиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **привела** is the past tense (feminine) of **привести** (to bring (someone with)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **привести**: to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. exercises.prompt: A spark caused the gunpowder to explode.

exercises.why: **проходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **проходить** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **пройти**. present: я прохожу́ · ты прохо́дишь · он прохо́дит · мы прохо́дим · вы прохо́дите · они прохо́дят. — Wiktionary, «проходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: My cold is on the way out.
exercises.context: **про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
